Map the interval I_k for k>=2 continuously and onto C_(k-1) in the next phase, and I_1/isolated singletons/p to its distinguished point. An interval-to-interval forward step strictly decreases index, so every exact orbit reaches the distinguished m-cycle. Conversely arbitrary backward depth is available through increasing source interval indices; preimages approach distinguished points. One epsilon-jump from that cycle to a deep predecessor yields chains between any two points, with exact phase congruence. Theorem A of Garcia Guirao transfers the continuous chain-transitive cyclic map to a triangular omega-limit realization. Continuity at p follows from all components outside a finite prefix converging to p; isolated components have no other continuity obstacles. The proof establishes the infinite case directly, not via finite sampling.
